quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Say the prefix alone, then add the rest. Does the prefix change its voicing when a voiced consonant follows?
quests.explanation: 'Disguise' has /s/ in the middle, even though a voiced /g/ follows: /dɪsˈgaɪz/. The prefix dis- keeps its voiceless /s/. Voicing it gives 'dizguise'. The word ends in /z/, so a voiceless /s/ in the middle and a voiced /z/ at the end sit in the same word.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'di', hiss with your tongue tip near the ridge and no voice, then lift the back of your tongue for 'g' and finish with 'eye-z'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The X stands for two sounds here, and a stressed vowel follows. Which of the two is the target, and is it voiced?
quests.explanation: 'Exaggerate' has /z/ in the middle: /ɪgˈzædʒəreɪt/. X is /gz/ before a stressed vowel, as in 'exam' and 'exist'. Using /s/ gives 'eksaggerate'. The word also has /dʒ/ right after it, so two voiced sounds sit next to each other.
quests.mouthPosition: Let a voiced hiss begin the stressed syllable, tongue tip near the ridge, then flow on into 'zaj'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: A lip stop sits before a hiss. Does your voice stay on through the lip closure?
quests.explanation: 'Absence' has /b/ before /s/: /ˈæbsəns/. The /b/ is voiced even though a hiss follows. Using /p/ gives 'apsence'. The spelling ABS is /æbs/, as in 'absolute'.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'a', close both lips with voice on, release into the hiss of 'sense', and finish with 'ns'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: After the weak first syllable, do the lips close, or does the tongue tip lift for the middle consonant?
quests.explanation: 'Tomorrow' has /m/ at the start of the stressed syllable: /təˈmɒroʊ/. The lips close and the hum goes through the nose. Using /n/ gives 'tonorrow'. The syllable after it contains /r/, which the tongue prepares for as the lips open.
quests.mouthPosition: Straight after the weak 'tuh', close your lips and hum through your nose, then open into the stressed 'mor' with the tongue pulling back for 'r'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Mark the stressed syllable. The nasal starts it. Where does the tongue touch?
quests.explanation: 'Pronounce' has /n/ at the start of the stressed syllable: /prəˈnaʊns/. The tongue tip touches the ridge and voiced air passes through the nose. Using /ŋ/ gives 'prong-ounce'. The word ends with /ns/, a second tongue-tip nasal plus a hiss.
quests.mouthPosition: The stressed syllable begins with the tongue tip on the ridge and a hum, then the 'ow' glide.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The X hides two sounds. Which one comes first, and does it let your voice join in?
quests.explanation: 'Oxygen' has /k/ in the middle, the first half of the X: /ˈɒksɪdʒən/. The /k/ is voiceless and puffed, followed straight away by a hiss. Using /g/ gives 'ogsygen'. After a stressed vowel, X is /ks/, not /gz/.
quests.mouthPosition: After the stressed 'ox', lift the back of your tongue for 'k', let the hiss follow immediately, then finish with 'ih-jen'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The first part of the word is 'further'. Compare its TH with the one at the start of 'thin'. Same or different?
quests.explanation: 'Furthermore' has /ð/ in the middle: /ˈfɜːrðərmɔːr/. 'Further' uses the voiced th, not the /θ/ of 'thin'. Using /θ/ gives a stiffer, breathy middle. The word ends in /m/ plus an r-coloured vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: In the middle of the word, the tongue tip meets the back of the upper teeth with voice on, then the lips close at the end for 'm'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Say the ending alone, '-riage'. Does the final sound begin with the tongue pressing the roof, or just brushing past it?
quests.explanation: 'Marriage' ends in /dʒ/: /ˈmærɪdʒ/. The ending is a seal and a voiced hush. Using /ʒ/ gives 'marrizh'. The same -age pattern gives 'carriage' and 'package'.
quests.mouthPosition: In the last beat, press the tongue front to the roof behind the ridge with the voice humming, and let it relax into a short buzzy hush.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Mark the stressed syllables. In the second syllable, is the tongue forward between the teeth, or the lip on the teeth?
quests.explanation: 'Enthusiastic' has /θ/ after the nasal: /ɪnˌθjuːziˈæstɪk/. The tongue tip slides forward from the ridge to between the teeth. Using /f/ gives 'enfusiastic'. The word also has /z/ later, so both a hiss and a buzz appear.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'in', slide your tongue tip forward between your teeth for a soft 'th', then glide up into 'yoo' and on.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word is made of two words you know, but the sound isn't what the spelling shows. What closes the lips in the middle?
quests.explanation: 'Cupboard' has /b/ in the middle: /ˈkʌbərd/. The P merges into the next sound and disappears. Saying /p/ gives 'cup-board', a spelling pronunciation. The middle lip closure is voiced.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'ku', close your lips with voice on for 'b' and release into the weak 'erd'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: A hard G follows the nasal. Where is the tongue as the nasal hums?
quests.explanation: 'Linguistic' has /ŋ/ before /gw/: /lɪŋˈgwɪstɪk/. The back of the tongue is raised for the nasal and stays for the /g/. Using /n/ gives 'lin-gwistic'. The word also has /gw/ and /st/ clusters to manage.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'li', raise the back of your tongue and hum through your nose, release into 'g', round your lips for 'w', then 'is-tik'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word begins with a consonant that isn't made by the lips alone. Check for contact between teeth and lip.
quests.explanation: 'Vowel' begins with /v/: the lip on the teeth with a buzz: /ˈvaʊəl/. Using /w/ gives 'wowel'. The word is just /v/, a glide, and an /l/.
quests.mouthPosition: Open with lower lip touching upper teeth and a buzz, then drop your jaw into 'ow' and finish with the tongue-tip 'l'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE LAST CONSONANT SOUND IN THE FINAL CLUSTER
quests.hint: Think about the stops just before the final sound. Do they pass voice on to it?
quests.explanation: 'Attempts' ends in /mpts/: hum, silent /p/, silent /t/, hiss. Only the /m/ is voiced, so the hiss stays voiceless. Using /z/ gives 'attemptz'. Many speakers drop the /p/ or /t/; keeping both makes the word clearer.
quests.mouthPosition: After the 'm' hum, close your lips with no voice for 'p', tap the tongue tip for 't', and hiss.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE LAST CONSONANT SOUND IN THE FINAL CLUSTER
quests.hint: After the tongue-tip stop, the word ends in a plural S. Voiced or voiceless?
quests.explanation: 'Hundreds' ends in /dz/: the voiced /d/ pulls the plural S to a voiced /z/: /ˈhʌndrədz/. Using /s/ gives 'hundrets'. The cluster /ndr/ in the middle also needs a clear tongue-tip closure.
quests.mouthPosition: Once the weak 'ruh' is said, close the tongue tip on the ridge with voice on for 'd', then release into a buzzing 'z'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE LAST CONSONANT SOUND IN THE FINAL CLUSTER
quests.hint: The ending has three consonants. Which sound is last, and is it voiced?
quests.explanation: 'Exempt' ends in /mpt/: hum, silent /p/, silent /t/: /ɪgˈzɛmpt/. The X is /gz/ at the start. Using /d/ gives 'exempd'.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'ig-zem', close your lips with no voice for 'p', then tap the tongue tip on the ridge for a silent 't'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: After a tongue-tip stop, -ed becomes a short syllable. What closes it?
quests.explanation: 'Disappointed' ends in /ɪd/: the base ends in /t/, so -ed adds a short syllable that finishes with a voiced /d/. Using /t/ gives 'disappointit'. The word also has /nt/ in the middle, so the tongue tip stops twice.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'point', slip in a short 'ih', then close the tongue tip on the ridge with voice on to end.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The base word ends in a hiss. What does -ed do after a hiss?
quests.explanation: 'Increased' ends in /st/: after the voiceless /s/, -ed is /t/: /ɪnˈkriːst/. Using /d/ gives 'increasd'. The spelling shows -eased, but the sound is just /st/.
quests.mouthPosition: Following the long 'ee', hiss with no voice and tap the tongue tip for a silent 't'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The ending follows a voiced hush. What does -ed do?
quests.explanation: 'Arranged' ends in /dʒd/: after the voiced /dʒ/, -ed is /d/: /əˈreɪndʒd/. Using /t/ gives 'arrangt'. With the nasal before the /dʒ/, the ending has three voiced consonants in a row.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'uh-rayn', seal your tongue behind the ridge with voice on, release into a buzzy hush, then close the tongue tip for a voiced 'd'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: There's a silent letter in the middle. Which sound do the lips make?
quests.explanation: 'Plumber' has /m/ in the middle; the B is silent: /ˈplʌmər/. Pronouncing the B gives 'plum-ber'. The word begins with /pl/, so the opening is a cluster.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'plu', close both lips and hum through your nose, then finish with 'er'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word ends in -ght. Which sound closes it: a stop, or soft air?
quests.explanation: 'Height' ends in /t/: /haɪt/. The GH is silent and the final T is a stop. Using /θ/ gives 'heighth', a slip influenced by 'width' and 'length'.
quests.mouthPosition: Straight after the 'eye' glide, tap the tongue tip on the ridge for a silent 't'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word ends in -gn. Which sound do you actually hear at the end?
quests.explanation: 'Campaign' ends in /n/: /kæmˈpeɪn/. The G is silent, as in 'sign' and 'foreign'. Pronouncing the G gives 'cam-pain-g'. The word also has /m/ and /p/ in the middle.
quests.mouthPosition: After the 'ay' glide, touch the tongue tip to the ridge and hum through your nose.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Compare with the word 'south'. Does the middle consonant of this word match the end of that one?
quests.explanation: 'South' ends in /θ/, but 'southern' has /ð/ in the middle: /ˈsʌðərn/. The th becomes voiced. Using /θ/ keeps the 'south' sound and breaks the pattern. The word ends with /n/.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'suh', let the tongue tip rest against the back of the upper teeth with voice on; the air hums past, then the word ends on 'ern'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Mark the stressed syllable. The target begins it. Where is the tongue tip?
quests.explanation: 'Authority' has /θ/ at the start of the stressed syllable: /ɔːˈθɒrɪti/. The tongue tip slides between the teeth for a soft voiceless stream. Using /s/ gives 'ausority'. The /θ/ is followed by /r/, so the tongue moves back quickly.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'aw', slide your tongue tip between your teeth, then pull it back for 'r' and finish with 'ih-tee'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Between two vowels, does the tongue seal against the ridge, or let air flow at the teeth?
quests.explanation: 'Gathering' has /ð/ in the middle: /ˈgæðərɪŋ/. Voiced air flows between the tongue and the teeth. Using /d/ gives 'gaddering'. The -ing ending needs /ŋ/ at the back of the tongue.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'ga', rest your tongue tip against the back of your upper teeth with voice on, then glide through 'er' into 'ing'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: PH stands for one sound here. Is it voiced?
quests.explanation: 'Sophisticated' has /f/ in the second syllable, spelled PH: /səˈfɪstɪkeɪtɪd/. The /f/ is voiceless. Using /v/ gives 'sovisticated'. The word ends with -ed after /t/, so the ending is /ɪd/.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'suh', rest your top teeth on your bottom lip and blow a voiceless stream into 'fis'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The X is followed by a stressed vowel. Is the second sound of the X voiced?
quests.explanation: 'Anxiety' has /z/ in the middle: /æŋˈzaɪəti/. X is /gz/ before a stressed vowel, and here the /g/ has merged into the nasal /ŋ/. Using /s/ gives 'angsiety'. Compare 'anxious', where the X is /kʃ/.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'ang', put the tongue tip near the ridge with voice on and buzz into the stressed 'zy'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The middle sound is spelled -si-. Is it voiced?
quests.explanation: 'Confusion' has /ʒ/ in the middle: /kənˈfjuːʒən/. The -sion after a vowel is voiced, as in 'vision' and 'decision'. Using /ʃ/ gives 'confushun'. The /f/ earlier in the word is voiceless; the /ʒ/ is voiced.
quests.mouthPosition: Shape your mouth for a hush, lips slightly rounded, and keep the vocal cords buzzing through the middle sound.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word is long and full of silent letters. Between the 't' and the 'w', which sound sits? Is it voiced?
quests.explanation: 'Straightforward' has /f/ in the middle: /ˌstreɪtˈfɔːrwərd/. It stacks several skills: the /str/ opening, a silent GH, a /t/ right before the /f/, and a final /d/. The /f/ is voiceless, so the voice has to switch off straight after the /t/. Using /v/ gives 'straightvorward'.
quests.mouthPosition: Hiss forward, tap 't' and pull back for 'r'. After the 'ay' glide, close for 't' and move straight into a voiceless lip-teeth 'f' before 'orward'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Count the voiceless sounds in the last syllable. Does the ending carry voice?
quests.explanation: 'Statistics' ends in /ks/: /stəˈtɪstɪks/. The /k/ is voiceless, so the final S is voiceless too. The word has /st/ three times, so each hiss and stop needs a quick, light contact. Using /z/ gives 'statistigz'.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'tis-ti', lift the back of your tongue for a silent 'k' and release straight into a thin hiss.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE FIRST CONSONANT SOUND IN THE OPENING CLUSTER
quests.hint: Say the opening cluster in slow motion. Does the tongue tip start between the teeth, or on the ridge?
quests.explanation: 'Throughout' begins with /θr/: the tongue tip starts between the teeth and pulls back for /r/. Using /t/ gives 'troughout'. The word also ends in /t/, so /θ/ and /t/ frame it. The GH in the middle is silent.
quests.mouthPosition: Put your tongue tip lightly between your teeth, pull it back for 'r' without stopping the air, glide into 'oo-ow', and close the tongue tip on the ridge for the final 't'.
